case.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
case.limits: The court leaned on the shooter's independent criminal act as a superseding cause. A system that interacts, personalises and responds in the moment is harder to cast as inert media, and current cases are testing precisely that seam.
case.holding: Makers of video games and films owed no duty of care for a school shooting allegedly influenced by their content, the crime was not sufficiently foreseeable, and intangible media content is not a product for strict liability.
case.why_ai_cites_it: The media-violence litigation of the 1990s produced the defense playbook now reused for AI harms: no duty to unforeseeable victims of a user's acts, superseding criminal conduct, and content-is-not-a-product. Chatbot harm suits are answered with this case's structure almost paragraph for paragraph.

reading.body:
The Sixth Circuit's 2002 ruling in *James v. Meow Media* gave defendants a three-part defense structure, no duty to unforeseeable victims, superseding criminal conduct by a third party, and content classified outside product liability, that is now reproduced almost verbatim in AI harm litigation.

The logic of the holding rested on treating the media as inert and the shooter's act as the real cause. That framing was plausible for films and video games, which do not adapt to a user in real time. The court's own caveat in this record acknowledges the seam: a system that personalises and responds in the moment is harder to characterise as passive, and that distinction is precisely what four live suits against Character Technologies are now pressing.

What the data does not resolve is whether any court has yet accepted or rejected the *James* framework when applied to an interactive AI system rather than static media. The four linked cases are active, not decided. The record here covers doctrine and posture, not outcome, so the defense playbook's durability against chatbot-specific facts remains an open question.

section.name: AI Case Law: The Precedents Behind the Defenses
